subject: Adaptor compatibility and backpatch plan (Unity Labs)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@unitylabs.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood adaptor: request for grace period & backpatch plan

Hi Marcus / Vanessa / Laura,

Thanks for taking a look. Quick background: Unity Labs will ship Engine 4.2.0 in mid-November which contains breaking changes to the event routing layer our customers' tooling integrations (including your Unity-adaptor) depend on. We expect a small number of our mutual customers to upgrade quickly.

Our ask: can Redwood commit to a 6-month compatibility window for your current adaptor API (v1.x) or, alternatively, provide a backpatch schedule and an exemption to your semver enforcement so we can co-maintain a shim? Were trying to avoid customers seeing runtime errors and to give ISVs time to port.

Included: compatibility matrix (unity-compat-matrix.csv) that maps Engine versions to the affected client calls.

High-level asks:
- Either a 6-month pinned v1 stability window OR an agreed backpatch cadence (we can cost-share).
- A weekly technical sync during the first 60 days to prioritize fixes.
- An engineer contact for integration test runs and a JIRA ticket we can reference.

We're happy to sign an NDA or process a simple MSA amendment if legal needs it. Samira (Engineering Partnerships) will coordinate on our side.

Attachments: unity-compat-matrix.csv

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, Unity Labs
samira@unitylabs.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@unitylabs.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood adaptor: request for grace period & backpatch plan

Samira — thanks for the heads up and the matrix. Ill loop in Partnerships and Eng leadership.

Vanessa / Laura / Kim: can product/eng review the matrix and confirm what we can support operationally (6-month pin vs backpatch cadence)? Id prefer a proposal that minimizes customer breakage but also keeps team focus manageable.

I can set up a weekly 30-min sync starting next Wed if that works for everyone.

Marcus
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@unitylabs.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood adaptor: request for grace period & backpatch plan

Hi Samira / team,

Appreciate the early notice and the matrix — super helpful. From a GTM/PS perspective wed also like to align on customer comms and any joint Q&A. Operationally, two pragmatic paths look feasible to me:

Option A — 3 month grace + partnership MAP (low maintenance):
- Redwood pins v1.x for 3 months and does high-priority compatibility patches for critical regressions only.
- Unity commits to a migration checklist, a test harness, and customer outreach plan.
- Weekly sync to triage reported failures.

Option B — co-maintained backpatch cadence (higher effort, longer runway):
- Redwood provides backpatches for 4.x minor drops for 6 months, on a defined SLA cadence (e.g., 2-week turnaround for P1 regressions).
- Costs for dedicated engineering time are shared; we can run a quick estimate.

To move forward:
- Samira, can you populate the matrix with: 1) repro steps for top 5 failing calls, 2) a minimal test harness, and 3) a preferred target customer list for phased migration?
- Laura / Kim, can Eng provide a back-of-envelope for the cost and headcount needed under Option B? Id like to avoid committing to 6 months of full support unless we have the resources.

Ill set up the first sync for Wed 11/10 10:00 PT unless someone objects.

—Vanessa
Director, Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira@unitylabs.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood adaptor: request for grace period & backpatch plan

Thanks — digging in on the matrix now. A few technical notes and a request for what we need to estimate effort accurately: 

1) Scope: give us the exact public surface (API endpoints / client calls) affected. The matrix is good but we need concrete failing unit/integration tests.
2) Test harness: we can run the harness in our CI if you provide it as a Docker image + a short runbook. That speeds validation and reduces manual triage.
3) Semver exemption: we can evaluate an exemption for the adaptor package, but wed need Unity to sign an integration SLA (lightweight) that commits to publishing migration notes and a customer outreach plan.
4) Backpatching: our initial read is that supporting Engine 4.2.x compatibility for all existing v1.x customers for 6 months is a non-trivial lift (~2 FTEs for 3 months for full coverage). I attached a quick cost sketch (redwood-backpatch-cost-estimate.xlsx). If we limit to top-10 customers and agreed P1 calls only, the estimate drops significantly.

Please include the top customer list and label P1/P2/P3 failures in the matrix. If you can get the harness and repro steps by 11/16, we can provide a firm commitment on scope and cadence by 11/23.

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 10:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Samira / team,
> 
> Appreciate the early notice and the matrix — super helpful. From a GTM/PS perspective wed also like to align on customer comms and any joint Q&A.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager (Integrations), Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Samira Khan <samira@unitylabs.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood adaptor: request for grace period & backpatch plan

Thanks all — this is helpful. We agree to the following and will deliver on our side:

- Unity will provide the Dockerized test harness + runbook and label the top P1 calls by 11/16. (attachments: unity-test-harness.zip)
- We will populate the compatibility matrix with repro steps and a prioritized customer list by 11/16.
- We can accept a targeted backpatch commitment for the top-10 customers and P1 calls; wed like Redwood to commit to a 2-week SLA for P1 fixes during the 3-month window.
- Unity Legal will prepare a short compatibility letter (unity-legal-compat-letter.pdf) to support the semver exemption request; we can share it with your Legal if you want.

Well open JIRA ticket INF-4920 and attach the harness and matrix; please add any internal stakeholders to the ticket.

If the above looks right, lets proceed with the weekly sync next Wed (11/10) and reconvene after the initial validation the week of 11/23.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here — if we can land something pragmatic, it avoids a poor customer experience.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations, Unity Labs
Attachments: unity-test-harness.zip, unity-legal-compat-letter.pdf
